column4: The section's lexical image is explicit here: earth is made a “فِرَاشًا” and sky a “بِنَاءً”; rain and fruit in the same verse make this roof-and-floor a provisioned human dwelling.
“الْأَرْضَ قَرَارًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً” gives the paired ground and structure, then says God “صَوَّرَكُمْ”; the formed human completes the section's three-part house.
The section names the building root ب ن ي for the sky; “بَنَيْنَاهَا بِأَيْدٍ” directly stages God's construction of it.
The section's earth-floor image is explicit in “فَرَشْنَاهَا”; following 51:47, this verse supplies the lower, spread surface of the same cosmic house.
The section quotes this challenge to resurrection: “أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ السَّمَاءُ”; the sky's building is set against human creation as evidence for the Creator's power.
“رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا” completes the roof image and uses the same root س و ي that the section traces from sky to soul.
“وَالْأَرْضَ ... دَحَاهَا” continues the creation sequence with a spread earth, paired with the raised, leveled sky in 79:28.
After creating what is on earth, God turns to the sky and “فَسَوَّاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ”; this uses the section's finishing verb for the heavens themselves.
The section's third structure is a living human: “سَوَّاهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِ” joins proportioning the body with the spirit that gives it life.
Addressing each person, God says “خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ”; it directly echoes the section's formed and balanced nafs.
The human is proportioned and receives spirit: “سَوَّيْتُهُ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي,” the same body-and-life pairing as the section's nafs definition.
This account likewise says “فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ” before breathing the spirit into the human; it makes the formed person a living structure.
“فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ ... رَكَّبَكَ” describes God assembling a person in a chosen form, a concrete parallel to the section's built human frame.
“خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى” repeats the section's key finishing verb, here for the Creator's act of making creation proportionate.
The verse places the true creation of heaven and earth beside God's shaping humans and making their forms good, bringing the cosmic and human structures together.
“الْإِنسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ” specifically presents the human form as excellently proportioned, matching the section's completed nafs structure.
“الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا” makes the earth a spread bed, the lower surface in the section's tent-like house.
“وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا” gives mountains the tent-peg role that the section explicitly derives from its earth-and-tent image.
The earth is made “مَهْدًا” and routes are opened in it; the verse depicts a habitable ground under the sky, as in the section's floor image.
“جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا” directly pictures the earth as a laid-out cradle or bed for people.
“الْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًا” directly names the earth as a spread, carpet-like surface, matching the section's floor and rug senses.
The verse calls portable livestock-skin dwellings “بُيُوتًا”; this is the section's secondary dictionary image of a domed tent made from hides.
“السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَّحْفُوظًا” directly names the sky as a protected roof, the section's central gloss for the upper structure.
The verse asks how God built and adorned the sky, then says it has no “فُرُوجٍ”; this is the section's roof with no cracks.
“السَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ” is the raised roof invoked in an oath, directly matching the section's sky-as-ceiling definition.
God “رَفَعَ السَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا”: the raised roof has no visible pillars, clarifying how its construction differs from a tent's supports.
This pairs heavens “بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ” with firm mountains placed in earth; it contrasts the unsupported upper structure with the pegged, stabilized ground.
The layered heavens “طِبَاقًا” have no disparity in their creation, a specific account of the sky's ordered construction.
The inspection of the layered heavens ends with “مِن فُطُورٍ”; this verse sharpens the gapless-roof claim begun in 67:3.
“وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا” explicitly describes the heavens above as built, matching the section's ceiling structure.
After the heavens are formed in 41:11, this verse makes seven skies and adorns the lowest with lamps; it gives a concrete continuation of the constructed upper realm.
“وَإِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ” directs attention to the earth as a spread surface, the section's lower floor.
“السَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ” joins the raised roof to balance; this makes cosmic structure and proportion co-present as in the section's account of sawwā.
“وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ” continues the raised-heaven scene with earth laid out for living creatures, the floor beneath that roof.
“مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ” is a direct spread-earth formulation; its rivers and fixed mountains specify features placed on that surface.
“مَدَدْنَاهَا” directly describes the earth spread out, then mentions mountains and measured growth upon it, extending the floor image.
After the built sky in 50:6, this verse says “مَدَدْنَاهَا” of earth and places mountains and growth on it; its own contribution is the lower spread plane.
Between the leveled sky and spread earth, this verse darkens night and brings out daylight; it adds the sky's alternation to the same creation sequence.
Following the earth's spreading in 79:30, this verse brings its water and pasture forth; it shows what the laid-out ground yields.
“وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا” follows the spread earth with fixed mountains, a functional counterpart to the section's tent-pegs.
The next verse names the earth's yield as provision for people and livestock, completing the usable-ground scene begun in 79:30.
God makes “ظِلَالًا” and mountain shelters; this fits the section's named secondary sense of sky as what rises over and shades you.
The section explicitly gives the lexicographic gloss “what rises above and shades you”; this verse stages an extended “ظِلّ” as that covering.
The section's building-root dictionary entry calls the ribs of the chest “البواني”; “بَيْنِ الصُّلْبِ وَالتَّرَائِبِ” names the back and ribs in the human frame.
The root س و ي is used as “سَاوَى” for leveling between two mountain sides while building a barrier, a second concrete scene of construction and leveling.
The section's dictionary gloss connects sound human “بِنْيَة” with fitra; this verse explicitly names God's “فِطْرَتَ” upon which people are created.
The section glosses nafs as the spirit by which the body lives; this verse says God takes the “الْأَنفُسَ” in sleep and death, showing the soul-body relation at its boundary.
The argument from making the heavens and earth to the ability to create humans again directly develops the resurrection challenge cited in the section's 79:27 sequence.
This asks whether the One who created the heavens and earth can revive the dead, making cosmic construction evidence for human re-creation as in 79:27.
The verse argues that the Creator of heavens and earth can create people again; it extends the section's sky-versus-human creation challenge to resurrection.
The verse says the human becomes a clot, then “فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى”; the same root links a formed body to the section's nafs, though this passage emphasizes embryonic sequence.
Bones are clothed with flesh before a new creation; this gives a specific assembly of bodily parts behind the section's “building by joining parts” gloss.
“يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ” locates the shaping of human forms in the womb, a concrete setting for the section's formed human structure.
“خَلَقْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ” gives a creation-then-forming sequence for human beings, parallel to the section's formed nafs.
The next verse says the Creator “قَدَّرَ فَهَدَى”; its own contribution is measured guidance, extending 87:2's proportioned creation toward the section's balanced design.
The heavens are described as “طِبَاقًا,” layered above; this supplies a stacked-ceiling image alongside the section's roof.
God holds the sky from falling on earth; this gives the roof image a specific account of how the upper structure is kept over the ground.
God holds the heavens and earth lest they cease; the verse ties the two structures in the section's house image to God's sustaining act.
The earth is made “ذَلُولًا” for walking over; this is a specific inhabited-ground counterpart to the section's spread floor.
After earth is called a spread in 71:19, this verse names broad routes through it; it adds movement across the surface.
After 25:45 extends shade, this verse says it is gradually drawn back; its own contribution is the withdrawal that qualifies shade as a changing cover.
After sky and balance are paired in 55:7, this verse forbids transgressing the balance, carrying the section's proportion image into a stated limit.
The next verse commands a just measure; it gives the balance in 55:7 a concrete human practice, a bridge from formed proportion to measure.
Immediately before the section's quoted raised roof in 52:5 stands the “الْبَيْتِ الْمَعْمُورِ”; this row supplies the inhabited-house image beside the ceiling.
“غُرَفٌ مِّن فَوْقِهَا غُرَفٌ مَّبْنِيَّةٌ” pictures built rooms above rooms; it offers a specific stacked-house parallel to the section's image of the nafs as a third room.
Seven heavens and matching earths are created together; the verse expands the section's paired upper and lower cosmic structures into a corresponding set.
In an argument about resurrection, this verse sets stages of human formation beside rain reviving dead earth; it brings the section's formed person and spread ground into one scene.
The reply to the question about dead bones says the One who originated them first can revive them; 36:81 then supplies the sky-and-earth proof, while this row contributes the first-creation premise.
Firm mountains are placed lest earth sway with people; this is a functional parallel to the section's tent pegs fixing the ground.
Firm mountains are set in earth lest it shake, another explicit stabilizing role that sharpens the tent-peg image.
The Qur'an describes a building founded on piety versus one on a crumbling bank; read beside the section's formed nafs, it gives a specific moral extension to its house image.
Pharaoh orders Haman “ابْنِ لِي صَرْحًا,” a human tower-building counter-scene to the sky built by God; 40:37 specifies the intended reach toward heaven.
Pharaoh orders a tower of baked clay to look toward Moses' God; this is a human-built, earth-bound counter-image to the divine construction of the sky.
The section's dictionary form glosses nafs as the living body's rūḥ; this verse sets an epistemic boundary around “الرُّوحُ,” calling it of the Lord's command and human knowledge little.
The section defines earth as the body opposite the sky; this verse reverses that distinction at the origin by saying heaven and earth were joined and then parted.
Continuing the sky-and-earth scene after 50:7, this verse sends blessed water from the sky and grows gardens and grain; it connects the roof above to growth on the spread ground.
The same scene continues with tall date palms and layered fruit; its own contribution is growth rising from the earth described in 50:7.
This continuation calls the yield provision and says water revives a dead town; it links the spread earth to both sustenance and resurrection.
After earth is called a bed in 20:53, this verse directs people to eat from it and pasture their livestock, making its inhabitable surface concrete.
The earth laid out in 55:10 is shown bearing fruit and date palms; this verse continues the ground-as-floor image with its produce.
This next verse adds grain and fragrant plants to the produce on the earth laid out in 55:10.
The section's built roof is said to have no fissures, while this judgment scene says “السَّمَاءُ انفَطَرَتْ”; the same sky becomes split.
This is another specific reversal of the section's intact roof: “السَّمَاءُ انشَقَّتْ” at the end-time boundary.
The mountains used as tent pegs in 78:7 are here destined to be scattered; this verse begins the reversal of their anchoring role.
After mountains are questioned in 20:105, this verse says they are left level, undoing their peg-like fixing of the earth.
The next verse completes the leveled landscape: no crookedness or rise remains where mountains had served as anchors.
The same surah that calls mountains “pegs” in 78:7 later says they are set moving; the tent's fixed anchors are removed at judgment.
Mountains that seem fixed pass like clouds; this reverses their peg-like stability and shows the ground image at the judgment boundary.
The section's roof and shade imply a sheltering cover; this passage's “ظِلٍّ مِّن يَحْمُومٍ” is a smoky shade in punishment.
The next verse says that shade is neither cool nor noble, explicitly reversing the comfort suggested by an overhead shelter.
